title: Card Grading Companies Ranked (2026)
verdict: Card grading companies ranked for 2026: AGS first for measured, repeatable grades, then PSA for resale, CGC for price, Beckett for subgrades, TAG for modern cards and SGC for vintage.

Three of the big names, PSA, SGC and Beckett, are now tied to one owner. That does not make their grades worse, but it narrows the choice. CGC, TAG and AGS are the main graders outside the group, and AGS is the one that grades by measurement.

list: A grade from 1 to 10 with decimal precision.
Eight subgrades: centering, corners, edges and surface, front and back.
A 3D heightmap of the surface, color-coded from green to red.
High-resolution images and centering data for both sides.
A sealed PMMA slab with the cert number on the label.
A permanent online record, reachable by cert number or shared link.

ranking.fit: Collectors who want to see why a card got its grade, without paying by card value.
ranking.lacks: A younger slab. PSA holders still bring the highest resale prices on most cards.
ranking.note: Standard service is 20 business days or less. Faster bulk tiers run 10 and 5 business days. Payment is taken when grading is done.

ranking.fit: Modern card collectors who like the half-point scale.
ranking.lacks: Subgrades by eye, and 45 business days or more at the Base tier.

ranking.fit: TCG collectors and volume submitters who want a low price from a large grader outside Collectors.
ranking.lacks: No measured report behind the grade.

ranking.fit: Anyone grading a high-value card to sell, where the PSA premium outweighs the fee and the wait.
ranking.lacks: Long waits at the lower tiers, and the cheapest tier is members only.

ranking.fit: Modern card collectors who like a slab with no paper label.
ranking.lacks: Prices were not posted on its pricing page when we checked.

ranking.fit: Vintage sports collectors who like the black-insert holder.
ranking.lacks: A smaller buyer pool for modern TCG cards.

why: The grade comes from a machine, so it does not depend on who is on shift. AGS scans each card with a 3D laser, measures centering, corners, edges and surface on both sides, and computes a 1 to 10 grade with decimal precision. Scan it again and AGS says the number holds.
Ownership matters to some collectors. Collectors holds PSA and SGC and has a deal for Beckett. CGC belongs to Certified Collectibles Group. AGS is its own company, Automated Grading Systems Inc.
Nothing is locked in. No minimum order, no membership, no contract, and payment is taken when the cards are graded. A first order gets 20% off with code AGSNEW20.

faq.q: How are card grading companies ranked here?
faq.a: On consistency first, then evidence, price, turnaround, resale and terms. AGS is first, then PSA, CGC, Beckett, TAG and SGC. The publisher of this page owns AGS, which is disclosed in the footer.

faq.q: How does AI card grading work?
faq.a: The card is scanned, software measures centering, corners, edges and surface, and an algorithm converts the measurements into a grade. AGS uses a 3D laser scan of roughly 30 million data points per card. No human opinion sets the number.

faq.q: How much does AGS charge to grade a card?
faq.a: $18 per card at the standard rate, whatever the card is worth. Bulk orders of 30 or more TCG cards are $15 each at 20 business days, $20 at 10 or $30 at 5. Sports and non-TCG bulk is $3 more per tier.

faq.q: Is AGS a legitimate grading company?
faq.a: Yes. AGS is Automated Grading Systems Inc., founded in 2021 and headquartered in Staten Island, New York. It publishes a live population report and a cert lookup, and says it ranked third in TCG grading volume in 2026.

faq.q: Does grading increase a card's value?
faq.a: Often, not always. A high grade on a card in demand can multiply its price. A low grade can sell for less than the raw card. Look at sold prices for the grade you realistically expect.
